items.title: Sections with compact support in degree zero are the global sections vanishing near the complement
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors

items.difficulty_reason: For a proper scheme X over a field k, K in D^b_Coh(O_X) with H^i(K) = 0 for i < 0 and F = H^0(K), and a closed Z with complement U, the lemma asserts that H^0_c(U, K|_U) is the subset of H^0(X, F) consisting of those global sections of F which vanish in an open neighbourhood of Z (statement lines 9275-9312). The proof considers the map H^0_c(U, K|_U) -> H^0_X(X, K) = H^0(X, F) of Remark labelled remark-covariance-open-lower-shriek, replaces K by a bounded complex F^bullet with F^i = 0 for i < 0, and computes H^0_c(U, K|_U) as the limit of the H^0(X, I^n F^bullet) = Ker(H^0(X, I^n F^0) -> H^0(X, I^n F^1)) (proof lines 9294-9306). Artin-Rees, Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma labelled coherent-lemma-Artin-Rees, makes this the limit of the H^0(X, I^n F), so the arrow is injective with image the sections of F contained in I^n F for every n; that these are exactly the sections vanishing in a neighbourhood of Z follows from Krull's intersection theorem, Algebra, Lemma labelled algebra-lemma-intersect-powers-ideal-module-zero, applied to the stalks of F, with the function case recorded in Algebra, Remark labelled algebra-remark-intersection-powers-ideal (proof lines 9306-9312). Replacing the compactly supported group by a limit along the powers of the ideal and then reading the limit off the stalks via Krull is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.
